newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak, downside risk seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak, downside risk seen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended weak on Friday after falling below a key support level in early trade and dealers said the market looked susceptible to further declines.
"When it broke 18,800, more and more people wanted to go short," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract lost 370 points to end at 18,590 on healthy volume of 21,425 lots.
Dealers said the yen's continued gains versus the dollar prompted profit-taking in some export-related blue chips in the underlying cash market.

The Dow's overnight drop for the second straight session following Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's warning about a pre-emptive interest rate hike to check inflation also weighed on sentiment, dealers said.
"The Nikkei will be more sensitive to bad news than good news now," said the trader.
He said the March Nikkei was likely to test support at 18,350-18,400 in the short-term and a breach of that level could push it below 18,000.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 325.6 against its opening 323.0 on volume of 774 lots.
